questions.question: Select the sentence with no spelling errors.

options.text: He made several excursions in the tribal habitats there.
He made several excursions in the tribel habitats there.
He made several excrusions in the tribal habitats there.
He made several excursions in the tribal habetats there.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"excursions"** means a short journey or trip, especially one taken for pleasure or leisure. (यात्रा)

 
 
• **Example: **The family went on multiple **excursions** during their summer vacation.
 
 
 
• **"Tribal"** refers to something related to a tribe, which is a social group existing before the development of, or outside of, states. (जनजातीय)
 
 
• **Example: **They studied the customs of various** tribal **communities in the region.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2:** "Tribel" (जनजातीय) is a misspelling of "tribal".

 
 
• **Example:** Incorrect: He studied the tribel customs of the area.

 Correct: He studied the tribal customs of the area.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Excrusions" (यात्रा) is a misspelling of "excursions".
 
 
• **Example:** Incorrect: They went on several excrusions last summer.

 Correct: They went on several excursions last summer.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "Habetats" (आवास) is a misspelling of "habitats".
 
 
• **Example:** Incorrect: The animals live in various habetats.

 Correct: The animals live in various habitats.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option for the given blank.

Don't ___________ your energy on random things, and try to focus.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word** "waste"** appropriately fits the context of the sentence, which suggests not to spend energy on random things.
 
• **"Waste"** means to use or expend carelessly, which aligns with the idea of focusing energy rather than dispersing it.
 
• The other options** ("kick", "hold", "haste") do not fit the context as well as "waste" does.**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Don't **waste** your energy on random things, and try to focus."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "kick"** – This word does not fit the context of conserving energy.
 
• **Option 2: "hold"** – This word also does not fit the context as it suggests retaining rather than expending energy.
 
• **Option 3: "haste"** – This word means to hurry, which does not fit the context of wasting energy.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

Leave now; _________ you'll be late.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The conjunction "**otherwise**" is used to show what the result will be if a particular action is not taken or a condition is not met.
 
• In this context, "**otherwise**" is the most appropriate word to indicate that if you do not leave now, you will be late.
 
• The other options do not fit logically or grammatically into the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Leave now; **otherwise** you'll be late."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Until:** This word is used to indicate the time up to the point that something happens. It does not fit the context here.
 
• **If:** This word introduces a conditional clause. It does not fit the structure of the sentence.
 
• **Unless:** This word means except if. It also does not fit the context and sentence structure here.
